page.layout: One printed page: running head at top; below it a title line, a woodcut emblem picture filling the middle, then a verse text of six lines beneath with a large initial B; a signature mark at the foot right.

l.i: BElidas fingunt pertusa in dolia Gates
Nomine mutato, narratur fabula de te,
Ebrie, quae meias qui sine fine bibis.
Quin etiam hoc in te quadrat turba ebria,
Corpora quae fuerant, dolia facta tibi.

main_text.l: [Woodcut: a man with a barrel on his body pours water from a jug, beside a large tub into which a woman pours; figures in a courtyard.]

page.notes: The large initial reads "B" as printed, likely "D" for Danaides; the first word is set as printed "BElidas" (possibly "Danaides" in the original, read here as shown). Line "Ebrie, quae meias qui sine fine bibis" and "Gates" are doubtful; "quod sint" is a broken line as printed. Woodcut described, not transcribed.
